degrade_withheld: - **Font embedding** — `doc.EmbedFonts()` embeds the fonts a document names and does not embed — simple (`/Type1`, `/MMType1`, `/TrueType`) and composite (`/Type0`), written as indirect objects or directly in a page's resources, an annotation appearance, a tiling pattern, a Type 3 font's resources or `/AcroForm /DR` — from a face in a folder registered with `RegisterFontFolder` or `RegisterSystemFonts` — a TrueType face, or an OpenType-CFF (`.otf`) face whose CFF is name-keyed, embedded as `/FontFile3 /Type1C` under a `/Type1` font. A symbolic font (Wingdings, Symbol) that states no encoding is embedded from a face with a (3,0) symbol cmap and stays a symbolic `/TrueType`, its codes reaching glyphs through that cmap. The face is found by **name** — its PostScript name, or its family in the font's own weight and slant, so Word's `TimesNewRoman,Bold` finds Times New Roman Bold — never by which characters it covers, since embedding a face states that it *is* the font named. Each font is kept only when every code the document shows in it has a glyph in the face and a `/Widths` entry within 1/1000 em of the face's advance, so no text moves; otherwise it is put back exactly as it was and reported with the reason and the code that disagreed. The program is shrunk to the glyphs shown (`subset: false` keeps it whole), and `bundledStandard14: true` gives a Standard-14 font with no registered face the bundled metric-compatible Liberation substitute. A Type 1 (`.pfb`/`.pfa`) face is embedded as itself in `/FontFile`, re-emitted with binary eexec and its three lengths, checked against each shown code's glyph name and charstring width, and subset by erasing the glyphs not shown while every name stays defined. A composite font whose encoding is `Identity-H` gets a TrueType face as a `CIDFontType2` with a `/CIDToGIDMap` built from what each CID means — the font's `/ToUnicode`, else Adobe's published table for its character collection — and is kept only when every shown CID has a glyph and a `/W` width matching the face; another encoding is reported. A font written directly in a resource dictionary has no object number, so its report record names the pages that declare it. A run that embeds nothing leaves the document unmodified.

degrade_withheld: - **Tagged-PDF structure authoring** — `doc.CreateStructTree()` builds (idempotently) a `/StructTreeRoot` and marks the document Tagged; `root.Append(type, opts?)` / `element.Append(...)` grow the tree, with live setters for `Alt` / `ActualText` / `Lang` / `Title` / `Expansion` / `ID`, `SetType(type)` / `Type =` for the structure type itself (validated against the standard types and the `/RoleMap`, and rewriting the marked-content tag behind the element), `element.Remove()` detaches an element and its subtree, releasing its `/ParentTree` slots and untagging the content it marked without deleting any of it, `element.MoveTo(parent, index?)` re-parents an element and its subtree (materializing an inherited `/Pg` first, so its marked content keeps its page), `element.ReorderChildren(order)` permutes an element's children while leaving its own text where it was, `element.References` reads the element's `/Ref` entry — the structure elements it points at, which is how a `TOCI` names its target and how a footnote and its citations reference one another (note this is **not** `element.Ref`, which is the element's own object reference), `element.Namespace` reads and writes the standard structure namespace an element's type is drawn from, `root.Namespaces` lists those the tree declares, `root.DeclareNamespace(uri)` adds one, `Append(type, { ns })` authors in one — which is required for the PDF 2.0 types (`Aside`, `Title`, `Sub`, `Em`, `Strong`, `FENote`, `DocumentFragment`, `Artifact`), since those are not PDF 1.7 types and are rejected without it — and `RegisterRole(custom, standard)` for the `/RoleMap`. A type that is neither standard nor mapped is rejected with a `RangeError` rather than written — an arbitrary `/S` is how a tree comes to fail `ValidatePdfUa` in a way the author cannot see, and the check runs before anything is allocated, so a rejected call leaves the document byte-identical. Tag authored content by passing a `tag: StructElement` to `AddText` / `AddTextBlock` / `AddImage` — they emit `/<type> <</MCID n>> BDC … EMC` and wire the `/ParentTree` and element `/K` so the read model (`GetText`, `ElementFor`) reads it back. Tag annotations with `element.AddAnnotation(annot)` (`/StructParent` + `OBJR`), and mark hand-built vector content with `element.NextMcid(page)` + `PageGraphics.BeginMarkedContent` / `EndMarkedContent`. `doc.Lang = 'en-US'` sets the document default language. Vector producers — `AddBarcode` and `AddSVGObject` — take the same marking vocabulary: `alt` tags the drawing as a `/Figure` carrying that alternate text, `tag` places it under a `StructElement` you already hold, and `artifact: true` declares it decoration. With none of them the drawing is emitted unmarked and `ValidatePdfUa` reports `UntaggedContent` — only you know whether a given graphic carries meaning, so the library does not guess. `artifact` cannot be combined with `tag` or `alt`.

- **Accessibility auto-tagging** — `doc.AutoTag(opts?)` infers a `/StructTreeRoot` for an untagged document from page layout: headings by font-size clustering (the modal size is body text; larger distinct sizes rank `H1`..`H6`), paragraphs, and images as `Figure` (with `/Alt` from `opts.alt`) or `/Artifact` when undescribed. It marks the document Tagged (and, with `opts.title`, sets the title + `/ViewerPreferences /DisplayDocTitle`; `opts.lang` sets `/Lang`), returning per-type counts (`AutoTagReport`). Detected tables (via `GetTables`) are tagged as `Table > TR > TH/TD` — the first row of a multi-row table becomes a header row (`TH`, `scope` Column) and any `rowSpan`/`colSpan`/`summary` are carried into the table attributes; `opts.tables` (default true) toggles table detection. It is built on `element.MarkContent(page, region)`, which wraps existing page content in `/<Type> <</MCID n>> BDC … EMC` so `GetStructTree` / `GetText` read it back. Heuristic — a starting point for accessibility remediation, not a guarantee of semantic correctness; lists are a follow-up.

It also reports missing or wrong PDF/UA identification (`pdfuaid:part`) at BOTH parts, as a WARNING rather than an error — the reference profile tags every identification rule `minor`, so a document whose only defect is a missing claim still reports `Passed`. Note part 1 wants `pdfuaid:part 1` and states no `rev` requirement, unlike part 2. Authoring writes no `pdfuaid`: making a conformance claim on your behalf is not the library's business, so call `ConvertToPdfUa()` or `SetXmp({ pdfuaPart: 1 })` when you want one. Returns a `ValidationReport` with `Issues` / `Errors` / `Warnings` (each a `ValidationIssue` carrying a stable `rule` id, `severity`, ISO/Matterhorn `clause`, and the offending `element`/`page`) and a `Passed` flag (true when there are no errors). It also answers clauses 8.9 and 8.10 — annotations and forms: an Invisible or NoView annotation that is not an artifact, a markup annotation not enclosed by an `Annot` element or whose `/RC` disagrees with its `/Contents`, `/Ink`, `/Screen`, `/3D` and `/RichMedia` annotations with no `/Contents` and a rubber stamp with neither `/Name` nor `/Contents`, a `/Popup` that is tagged, a file attachment whose `/FS` states no `/AFRelationship`, the prohibited `/Sound`, `/Movie` and `/TrapNet` subtypes, a zero-size widget or a printer's mark that is not an artifact, a watermark outside an `Annot`, a page carrying annotations with no `/Tabs` (a warning), an annotation whose `/Contents` and enclosing `/Alt` differ, a field widget outside a `Form` element or sharing one with another widget, an `/XFA` packet, a widget with neither a label nor `/Contents`, a text field whose `/RV` has no matching `/V`, and a signature whose appearance paints a graphic with no `/Alt` to describe it (asked per annotation rather than per content item, which the source records as an approximation). And it answers clause 8.4.5 — fonts and CMaps: every rendered font embedded and defining every glyph it shows, glyph widths that agree between the font dictionary and the font program (within one unit of 1/1000 em), the four TrueType encoding rules (a non-symbolic face needs a `(3,1)` or `(1,0)` cmap subtable and a `MacRomanEncoding` or `WinAnsiEncoding` base with Unicode-resolvable `/Differences`; a symbolic one needs a `(3,0)` or `(1,0)` subtable and must state no `/Encoding`), a composite font whose `/CIDSystemInfo` disagrees with its encoding CMap, an embedded `CIDFontType2` with no `/CIDToGIDMap`, a CMap outside ISO 32000-2 Table 116 that is not embedded or that references one, an embedded CMap whose `/WMode` disagrees with its stream dictionary, a code that maps to no Unicode value or to one containing U+0000/U+FEFF/U+FFFE, and any `.notdef` a text-showing operator references.
